subject: MSA + Order Form: IP indemnity — notice/evidence thresholds and cap mechanics
messages:
From: Sara Ellis <sara.ellis@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> , Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Walker <tom.walker@acme-corp.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-06-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — IP indemnity carve-out and evidence thresholds

Hannah / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Our legal team has flagged the limitation of liability language — specifically we need an explicit carve-out from the liability cap for claims of third-party IP infringement tied to the indemnity obligations.

High level ask: we cannot accept a flat monetary cap that would apply to Redwood's IP indemnity obligations in cases of infringement. Our position is that (i) injunctive and other equitable relief should be available without monetary limitation; and (ii) monetary indemnity for IP claims should not be swallowed by the general liability cap.

That said, we're open to pragmatic guardrails to avoid abuse. To move things along, we proposed the following in the attached redline (ACME_redlines_MSA.docx):
- Carve-out: "Company's indemnity obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement shall not be subject to the limitation of liability set forth in Section X."
- Notice & proof: strict notice timing (30 days), detailed claim materials, and the customer's right to control the defense if Redwood declines to defend.
- Escrow/royalty fallback: if final adjudication awards statutory damages or royalties, the parties will enforce monetary award recovery (we proposed 12 months of average fees as a possible benchmark).

Before we get into specific clause drafting, can you confirm whether Redwood has a standard middle-ground you typically accept (royalty formula, escrow trigger, or injunctive carve-out)? Also — we'll need defense control, settlement approval rights, and cooperation covenants as part of any indemnity flow.

Tom and I are on a compressed timeline for procurement, so any counter-language by EOD tomorrow would help.

Best,
Sara
---
Sara Ellis
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Acme Corp

Date: 2026-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — IP indemnity carve-out and evidence thresholds

Sara — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. We appreciate Acme's desire for robust IP protection. We also need to balance exposure across our customer base; open-ended unlimited monetary exposure for IP indemnity is something we try to avoid.

Quick proposal from product + commercial side (for legal to validate):
- Equitable relief (injunctions, specific performance) explicitly preserved and not subject to the monetary cap.
- Monetary indemnity for third-party IP claims: excluded from the "general" liability cap but subject to a defined recovery mechanism: (i) Redwood's indemnity liability for monetary awards will be limited to the greater of (A) the general liability cap set forth in Section X, or (B) a royalty-based cap calculated as 12 months of average fees paid by Acme for the relevant product(s) at the time the claim is adjudicated.
- Burden & evidence: claim notice within 30 days, full claim materials, and a mandatory meet-and-confer before any settlement that would bind Redwood.
- Escrow: rather than a standing escrow, escrow of disputed funds post-final judgment (if either party requests) — avoids operational friction pre-judgment.

Rishi / Laura — can you weigh in on the legal side — specifically: (1) is the "greater of cap or royalty" workable from a risk allocation standpoint; (2) any suggested alternative language on mitigation / subrogation / proof that will protect Redwood without gutting Acme's rights?

If we can get to a short, defensible clause today, I can run it through procurement and send back to Sara for sign-off.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Ellis <sara.ellis@acme-corp.com>, Tom Walker <tom.walker@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — IP indemnity carve-out and evidence thresholds

Hannah / Laura / Sara,

Thanks — below is legal's recommended approach and a suggested clause we can drop into the MSA. Goal: preserve Acme's practical remedies while keeping Redwood's aggregate exposure bounded and ensuring appropriate notice/proof controls.

Key legal points:
1) Injunctive / equitable relief should be carved out of the monetary cap (we're fine with that).
2) For monetary indemnity arising from third-party IP claims, we can agree that such indemnity is not subject to the "general" limitation of liability but should be subject to a specific monetary ceiling tied to a royalty formula — this avoids unlimited exposure while addressing Acme's concern.
3) Require standard cooperation / mitigation steps and an express requirement that Acme must provide the court judgment / settlement paperwork to verify the award prior to Redwood paying.
4) Escrow only post-final-judgment if requested — we should resist pre-judgment escrow.
5) Subrogation / recovery: Redwood should retain subrogation rights to pursue reimbursement from third parties who caused the infringement.

Suggested clause (drop-in):
"For clarity, monetary damages awarded in connection with a final adjudication or settlement of a third-party claim that Company has proven is an infringement of its proprietary intellectual property shall not be subject to the limitation of liability set forth in Section X. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's aggregate monetary liability for such third-party IP claims shall not exceed the greater of (a) the limitation of liability amount set forth in Section X, or (b) a royalty cap equal to twelve (12) months of the average fees paid by Customer for the Redwood product(s) implicated by the claim, calculated based on the twelve (12) months preceding the date of final adjudication.

Customer must provide (i) written notice within thirty (30) days after Customer receives notice of a third-party claim, (ii) full copies of the claim materials, and (iii) prompt cooperation in the defense. Redwood shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any such claim, provided that Customer's prior written consent is required for any settlement that would impose an obligation on Customer or admit fault. Payment obligations under this paragraph shall be conditioned on Customer providing (and Redwood's receipt of) final judgment or settlement documentation verifying the award.

Escrow: the parties may agree to place funds into escrow only following final judgment or a binding settlement, upon written request by either party.

Subrogation: Redwood shall be entitled to exercise any rights of subrogation or contribution it may have against third parties who are responsible for the infringement.

Comments: this preserves equitable relief outside the cap, limits Redwood's monetary exposure to a predictable formula, and keeps the operational burden reasonable. If Acme needs a higher multiplier than 12 months, we can consider adjusting subject to reciprocal protections (e.g., waiver of certain consequential damages claims tied to use-case).

If Sara is OK with the structure, I'll draft a clean version of the clause and we can circulate for signature.

-Rishi

Hannah / Rishi — thanks, that draft is very close to what we had in mind. The carve-out + the royalty-cap approach is acceptable to Acme subject to internal procurement approval. A couple of small asks: (i) confirm the calculation will be demonstrably transparent (we may need to provide invoices to show average fees), and (ii) preserve Customer's right to assume or participate in defense if Redwood elects not to defend.

We can accept post-judgment escrow and the subrogation carve-out. Please circulate a clean clause and we can push the Order Form through DocuSign once procurement signs off.

I'll flag this to Tom; we should have sign-off by COB tomorrow.

Best,
Sara
